ECON_SCALE_DEF.label: Economies of scale (LRAC falls as output rises)

stages.name: Economies of scale (types)
stages.title: Economies of scale (types)
stages.sub: Distinguish the causes of falling long-run average cost, firm-specific and industry-wide.

steps.q: A bakery doubles its own output and invests in its own bigger ovens, and its average cost per loaf falls. Did this happen because the whole baking industry grew, or because of choices made inside this one bakery?
steps.right: Because of choices made inside this one bakery
steps.wrong: Because the whole baking industry grew
steps.hint: Only this bakery changed anything. Nobody else in the industry did.
steps.pre: Falling average cost caused by the firm's own growth is called

steps.q: A new rail line and specialist parts suppliers spring up because the whole car industry grew in one region, and every car firm there faces lower costs, even small ones that never grew. What caused this cost fall?
steps.right: The whole industry growing, not the firm growing
steps.hint: Even firms that stayed the same size benefited. What changed around them?
steps.pre: Falling average cost caused by the whole industry growing is called

steps.q: A supermarket chain grows large enough to order a million tins of beans at once instead of a thousand. Does the supplier charge the same price per tin, or offer a discount for the huge order?
steps.hint: Think about why wholesalers reward big orders.

steps.q: A small bakery's oven only bakes 50 loaves a day cheaply. A huge bakery's giant oven bakes 5,000 loaves a day at a much lower cost per loaf. What let the big bakery cut its cost per loaf?
steps.hint: This is about the equipment and production process, not about buying ingredients.

steps.prompt: Drag and drop the 4 key terms in the order they build on each other.

steps.q: A firm with 10 workers has one owner doing the accounts, hiring and marketing badly. A firm with 1,000 workers hires specialist accountants and HR managers, each doing one job well. What let the bigger firm cut its average costs this way?
steps.hint: This is about hiring specialists to run departments, not about buying inputs.
